_note: SSOT for the whole system. Scripts and the ingestion pipeline read this file at RUNTIME (fs.readFileSync / Get-Content), so editing this file is the only step needed to change the ontology - no code edits, no regeneration, no redeploy.
_domains: Top-level context buckets. A note belongs to exactly one. Relation vocabularies are keyed off this (see validRelationTypes).
_sectors: Entity attribute: coarse classification. Replace with whatever axis matters in your domain (e.g. Department, Team, Discipline).
_industries: Nested attribute: each sector allows only its own list. The validator rejects an industry that does not belong to the note's sector - this is what stops taxonomy drift.
_sources: Provenance of a note. Keeping this closed-vocabulary makes 'where did this claim come from' answerable by query instead of by memory.
_relations: Typed edges, bucketed by domain. This is the core of the ontology: a link is not just [[Note]], it is `analyzes:: [[Note]]`. The validator rejects a relation type that is not allowed for the note's domain. 'related' is the deliberate fallback in every bucket.
_aliasNote: Entity resolution. The ingestion pipeline reads this at runtime and rewrites relation targets from alias to canonical form, so [[Nvidia]] and [[NVIDIA]] cannot split into separate graph nodes. Exact-match only (never substring). Adding an alias is a one-line edit here - no pipeline change.
_hubs: Graph entry points. Each hub is a note in 000_Maps/ that a retrieval agent enters first, then traverses typed edges outward. Keep this small - hubs are doorways, not tags.
_folderMap: para_type -> destination folder. The ingestion pipeline uses this to decide where a generated note lands; the validator uses it to flag notes sitting in the wrong folder.
